top_signals.title: S&P 500 Falls as Inflation Worry Lifts Bond Yields
top_signals.summary:
A stalemate between the US and Iran boosted oil prices, dragging down stocks and bonds on concerns that elevated energy costs could fuel inflation and trigger further Federal Reserve rate hikes.
Drew Matus, Chief Market Strategist at Metlife Investment Management, discusses his market outlook. (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Central-bank repricing affecting yields, FX, liquidity and equities.

top_signals.title: Nvidia Up on Share-Repurchase Program; Mining Stocks Slide | Stock Movers
top_signals.summary:
On this episode of Stock Movers:

- Nvidia (NVDA) shares are up after the board of the leader in AI chips authorized an additional $150 billion under the company’s existing share-repurchase program. The move increases the total remaining amount authorized to $235 billion.
- Australia’s Northern Star Resources Ltd. rejected a takeover approach from South African rival Gold Fields Ltd. that could have created the second-largest gold miner, saying the A$38.7 billion ($27.1 billion) cash-and-shares offer undervalued its business.
- Roblox (RBLX) was cut to underperform from hold at Jefferies, which said the stock’s 30% rally since the gaming company’s second-quarter results in July reflects an overly optimistic view of bookings for the next 12 months. (Source: Bloomberg)
top_signals.why_it_matters: Commodity repricing impacting inflation expectations and industrial supply chains.

top_signals.title: Two-Month Trade Truce Extension Leaves Markets Cold After Trump-Xi Summit
top_signals.summary: Donald Trump gave Xi Jinping the full state-visit treatment in Washington, but markets were more interested in what the two leaders did not deliver. After three days of ceremony, an unusually warm presidential welcome and repeated pledges to stabilize relations between the world's two largest economies, the main economic outcome was a two-month extension of the existing U.S.-China trade truce, pushing its expiration from November 10 to January 10, 2027. That averted an immediate return to escalation, but fell short of the longer runway many investors…

top_signals.title: Germany's Gas Storage Sits at 57%, but VNG Says Winter Supply Is Covered
top_signals.summary: Thanks to diversified import capabilities, Germany doesn’t face a gas supply shortage despite record-low levels of natural gas in storage sites, according to one of the biggest German gas importers, VNG.  “Compared to 2022, the system is much more robust overall. We have more access to liquefied natural gas (LNG) and we have broadened our overall position in terms of sources of supply,” VNG’s chief executive officer Ulf Heitmueller told Reuters in an interview published on Monday. VNG imports natural gas from Norway…
